NHIS KNOWLEDGE BASE

Benefits Package — Chunked & Tagged

Source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits   |   Verified: April 2026

Component: NHIS Patient Rights & Entitlement Agent

What this document is

This is the Knowledge Base source document for the NHIS Patient Rights Agent. It takes the raw content from the NHIA benefits page and breaks it into individual 'chunks' — each one labelled with a metadata tag (ID, category, subcategory, source, date). These chunks are what get loaded into the vector database for the agent to search from when a patient asks a question.

Each coloured box below is one chunk. The green bar at the top of every chunk contains the metadata tag — copy this exactly when loading into your database.

Colour key:

Green = Coverage (covered services)

Red = Exclusions (NOT covered)

Amber = Notes / caveats

Blue = Contact / escalation

SECTION 1 — OUTPATIENT SERVICES

ID: coverage_opd_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:general]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

General outpatient conditions covered

NHIS covers consultations (including specialist reviews) and treatment for the following conditions at outpatient facilities:

Malaria

Acute respiratory tract infection

Diarrhoeal disease

Skin diseases and ulcers

Hypertension

Acute eye infections

Rheumatism

Anaemia

Intestinal worm disorders

Acute ear infections

Typhoid fever

Dental caries

Diabetes mellitus

Sexually transmitted infections (STIs)

Asthma

Other general and specialist conditions approved by the Minister of Health

ID: coverage_opd_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:investigations]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient investigations and diagnostics

The following diagnostic services are covered under NHIS for outpatient and specialist visits at accredited facilities. No co-payment is required for these.

Laboratory investigations (blood tests, urine tests, etc.)

X-rays

Ultrasound scans (for general and specialist outpatient care)

ID: coverage_opd_003   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:surgical]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient and day surgical operations

The following surgical procedures can be performed on an outpatient or day-case basis and are fully covered under NHIS:

Hernia repairs

Incision and drainage of abscesses

Excision of lumps

Haemorrhoidectomy (surgical removal of haemorrhoids)

ID: coverage_opd_004   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:hiv]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

HIV/AIDS — symptomatic outpatient treatment

NHIS covers HIV/AIDS symptomatic treatment for opportunistic infections at the outpatient level. This means treatment for the infections that arise because of HIV is covered. IMPORTANT: HIV antiretroviral (ARV) medicines themselves are NOT on the NHIS medicines list and are not covered — they are provided through the separate National AIDS Programme. Do not confuse symptomatic treatment of opportunistic infections with ARV coverage.

ID: coverage_opd_005   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:physiotherapy]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient physiotherapy

Outpatient physiotherapy is covered under NHIS at accredited facilities that offer this service. This includes standard physiotherapy sessions prescribed following injury, surgery, or a medical condition. Note: rehabilitation services other than physiotherapy are excluded (see exclusions section).

ID: coverage_opd_006   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:medicines]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient medicines

Medicines prescribed at outpatient visits are covered if and only if they appear on the official NHIS Medicines List. Two types of medicines are covered:

Prescription medicines on the NHIS Medicines List (551 medicines as of March 2025)

Traditional medicines approved by the Food and Drugs Board and prescribed by an accredited medical or traditional medicine practitioner

SECTION 2 — INPATIENT SERVICES

ID: coverage_inp_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:general]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

General inpatient care

When admitted to hospital, the following are covered in full under NHIS at any accredited facility:

General and specialist inpatient care

Laboratory investigations, X-rays, and ultrasound scans

Accommodation in the general ward

Feeding (where available at the facility)

Inpatient physiotherapy

Processing for blood and blood products

ID: coverage_inp_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:surgical]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Inpatient surgical operations

Most surgical operations performed on an inpatient basis are covered under NHIS. This includes major operations such as appendicectomy (removal of the appendix). The general principle is that surgery required to treat a covered condition is itself covered.

ID: coverage_inp_003   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:cancer]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Cancer — what is and is not covered for inpatients

NHIS has a specific and limited cancer coverage policy that patients must understand clearly:

COVERED: Cervical cancer treatment (fully covered)

COVERED: Breast cancer treatment (fully covered)

COVERED: Diagnosis and treatment of complications arising from other cancers — for example, anaemia caused by cancer, or bowel obstruction from a tumour

NOT COVERED: Treatment of cancers other than cervical and breast cancer (see exclusions)

ID: coverage_inp_004   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:medicines]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Inpatient medicines

Medicines administered during an inpatient stay are covered if they are on the NHIS Medicines List or are traditional medicines approved by the Food and Drugs Board and prescribed by an accredited practitioner. Any medicine not on the NHIS list is not covered and should not be charged to your NHIS card.

SECTION 3 — MATERNITY CARE

ID: coverage_mat_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: maternity:full]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Full maternity care — all stages covered at no cost

NHIS provides complete maternity care coverage at no cost to the patient. All of the following are covered in full at any NHIA-accredited facility. No co-payment is required at any stage:

Antenatal care (all antenatal visits throughout the pregnancy)

Normal delivery

Assisted delivery

Caesarean section (C-section) — fully covered, no additional charge

Post-natal care

ID: coverage_mat_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: maternity:dispute]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Maternity — common dispute scenario

If a facility asks you to pay for a delivery or caesarean section, this is incorrect. NHIS covers all maternity care including C-sections with no co-payment. If this happens: (1) Politely show your valid NHIS card and ask to speak with the administrator, (2) if unresolved, call the NHIA helpline on 0544446447. Do not leave the facility without escalating — you are entitled to this care at no cost.

SECTION 4 — ORAL HEALTH

ID: coverage_oral_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: oral_health]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Oral health services covered

The following dental services are covered under NHIS:

Pain relief — incision and drainage, tooth extraction, temporary pain relief

Dental restoration — simple amalgam fillings and temporary dressing

SECTION 5 — EYE CARE SERVICES

ID: coverage_eye_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: eye_care]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Eye care services covered

The following eye care services are covered under NHIS at accredited facilities:

Refraction (eye test to determine prescription for glasses)

Visual fields assessment

Eye scan

Keratometry (measuring the curvature of the cornea's anterior surface)

Cataract removal surgery

Eyelid surgery

SECTION 6 — EMERGENCY SERVICES

ID: coverage_emg_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: emergency]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

All emergencies are covered

NHIS covers all emergency health situations that demand urgent intervention. This is a broad, comprehensive category — you cannot be refused emergency care or asked to pay upfront because of your NHIS status. Emergency types covered include:

Medical emergencies

Surgical emergencies — including brain surgery or heart surgery due to accidents

Paediatric (children's) emergencies

Obstetric and gynaecological emergencies — including emergency caesarean sections

Road traffic accidents (RTAs)

Industrial and workplace accidents

ID: coverage_emg_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: emergency:brain_heart]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Important: brain and heart surgery — accidents vs. non-accidents

There is a critical distinction here that the agent must handle correctly. Brain surgery and heart surgery have two different coverage rules depending on cause: (1) Brain or heart surgery RESULTING FROM AN ACCIDENT is covered under the emergency category. (2) Brain or heart surgery NOT resulting from an accident (i.e. elective or disease-based) is listed under exclusions and is NOT covered. Always ask whether the cause is accident-related when advising on this.

SECTION 7 — EXCLUSIONS (NOT COVERED)

The following services and items are explicitly excluded from NHIS coverage. Telling a patient any of these are covered would be a critical error. Each exclusion is a separate chunk so the agent can retrieve them independently.

ID: exclusion_001   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: rehabilitation]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Rehabilitation (other than physiotherapy)

Rehabilitation services are excluded from NHIS, with the single exception of physiotherapy. This means services such as occupational therapy, speech therapy, and other rehabilitation programs are not covered.

ID: exclusion_002   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: appliances]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Appliances and prostheses

Medical appliances and prosthetic devices are not covered. This includes: optical aids (glasses, contact lenses), hearing aids, orthopaedic aids (braces, splints, artificial limbs), and dentures.

ID: exclusion_003   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: cosmetic_surgery]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Cosmetic and aesthetic surgery (with one exception)

Cosmetic surgeries and aesthetic treatments are not covered. EXCEPTION: Reconstructive surgery such as that performed on burns patients IS covered under NHIS. If a patient asks about cosmetic surgery, the answer is no — but if they ask about burns reconstruction or medical reconstructive surgery, the answer may be yes.

ID: exclusion_004   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: hiv_arvs]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: HIV antiretroviral (ARV) medicines

HIV antiretroviral medicines are explicitly excluded from the NHIS Medicines List and are not covered by NHIS. They are provided through the separate National AIDS Programme. Important distinction: treatment of HIV-related opportunistic infections (e.g. treating TB in an HIV patient) IS covered at the outpatient level — but the ARV drugs themselves are not.

ID: exclusion_005   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: assisted_reproduction]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Assisted reproduction

Assisted reproduction procedures are not covered. This includes artificial insemination (IVF and other fertility treatments) and gynaecological hormone replacement therapy.

ID: exclusion_006   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: echocardiography]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Echocardiography

Echocardiography (a painless test that uses sound waves to create moving pictures of the heart, giving information about its size, shape, and function) is not covered under NHIS.

ID: exclusion_007   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: photography]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Clinical photography

Clinical photography — photographs taken in clinics or hospitals to give visual records of a patient's condition and operations for tracking treatment progress in medical files — is not covered under NHIS.

ID: exclusion_008   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: angiography]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Angiography

Angiography — a procedure where a dye is injected into the blood vessels and an X-ray or photograph of the vessels is taken to assess blockages or abnormalities — is not covered under NHIS.

ID: exclusion_009   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: orthoptics]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Orthoptics

Orthoptics — the diagnosis and treatment of defective eye movements and coordination (e.g. for squint/strabismus correction therapy) — is not covered. Note: general eye care such as cataract removal and eyelid surgery IS covered.

ID: exclusion_010   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: dialysis]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Dialysis for chronic kidney failure

Dialysis for chronic kidney failure is explicitly excluded from NHIS coverage. This is an important and commonly asked question — patients with chronic renal failure cannot use NHIS to pay for dialysis sessions. Note: as of 2024, there were government announcements about limited dialysis additions — always verify the current policy before advising, as this may have been updated.

ID: exclusion_011   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: brain_heart_noaccident]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Heart and brain surgery (non-accident)

Heart and brain surgery that does not result from an accident is not covered. Only brain surgery or heart surgery that directly results from a road traffic accident, workplace accident, or other traumatic accident is covered under the emergency category.

ID: exclusion_012   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: cancer_general]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Cancer treatment (except cervical and breast)

Cancer treatment is only covered for cervical cancer and breast cancer. Treatment for all other types of cancer — including prostate cancer, lung cancer, colon cancer, liver cancer, lymphoma, leukaemia, and all others — is not covered. Diagnosis and treatment of complications arising from any cancer (e.g. anaemia, obstruction) IS covered.

ID: exclusion_013   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: organ_transplant]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Organ transplantation

Organ transplantation procedures of any kind are not covered under NHIS. This includes kidney transplants, liver transplants, heart transplants, and all other organ or tissue transplant procedures.

ID: exclusion_014   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: non_nhis_medicines]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Medicines not on the NHIS Medicines List

Any medicine that does not appear on the official NHIS Medicines List is not covered and cannot be charged to your NHIS card. The 2025 list contains 551 medicines described by their generic (INN) names. If a pharmacy tries to charge you for a medicine, check whether its generic name is on the list. Branded versions of listed medicines should still be dispensed — the patient should not pay if the generic equivalent is on the list.

ID: exclusion_015   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: treatment_abroad]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Diagnosis and treatment abroad

Any medical diagnosis or treatment sought outside Ghana is not covered by NHIS. NHIS only covers services delivered within Ghana at NHIA-accredited facilities.

ID: exclusion_016   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: medicals]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Medical examinations for non-clinical purposes

Medical examinations carried out for purposes other than treatment are not covered. This includes: employment medicals, school admission medicals, visa application medicals, and driving licence medicals.

ID: exclusion_017   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: vip_ward]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: VIP ward accommodation

VIP ward accommodation is not covered under NHIS. NHIS covers general ward accommodation only. If a patient chooses to be admitted to a VIP or private room, the additional cost is their personal expense.

ID: exclusion_018   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: mortuary]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Mortuary services

Mortuary services are not covered under NHIS. Families of deceased patients are responsible for mortuary fees.

SECTION 8 — CONTACT DETAILS & ESCALATION

ID: contact_001   [category: disputes]  [subcategory: contact_nhia]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NHIA official contact details

Use these contacts to report disputes, wrongful charges, or denial of service:

Phone: (0) 302 238136 / 233255 / 216970 / 241690

Patient helpline: 0544446447 (for members experiencing difficulties)

Email: info@nhia.gov.gh

Address: No. 36, 6th Avenue, Opposite AU Suite, Ridge Residential Area, Accra

SECTION 9 — HOW TO CONVERT THIS TO JSON

Once you have reviewed and verified all chunks above, you will convert this document into a JSON file for loading into the vector database. Below is the exact format to use for each chunk. Copy the metadata from the green bar of each box above.

},
